items.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq rise ahead of historic Anthropic trading debut
items.take: Anthropic begins trading on the Nasdaq this morning under ticker ANT after pricing at $83 a share, above the marketed $70-78 range, the largest IPO in history at about $81 billion. The deal is reviving the battered AI trade before the bell, with Nasdaq futures up over 1.5% and Broadcom up nearly 3%.

items.title: Dow drops more than 500 points; S&P 500 falls for fifth day as Nvidia sells off
items.take: Nvidia slid 3% again Wednesday, a fifth straight losing day, dragging the S&P 500 to its fifth consecutive decline, while UnitedHealth's 10% plunge pushed the Dow down more than 500 points. The chipmaker's quarter beat estimates, so the selloff is about leadership uncertainty after Jensen Huang's resignation, not the numbers.

items.title: Walmart (WMT) Q3 2026 earnings
items.take: Walmart beat on both lines ($188.8 billion revenue, 65 cents adjusted EPS) and raised its full-year outlook for the third time this year, on 23% e-commerce growth heading into the holidays. The consumer bellwether gives the market one more reason to feel good besides the Anthropic IPO.

items.title: Fed Saw Need to Keep Raising Interest Rates Despite Holding Steady in October
items.take: Minutes from the Fed's October meeting show most officials saw further rate increases as needed, calling inflation pressures 'broad based' and flagging high energy prices. Markets read it as hawkish: gold fell to its lowest in over a year, silver to a 52-week low, and the 10-year yield sits near 5.1%.

items.title: Futures Rip As Anthropic IPO Frenzy Revives AI Trade, Asian Chips Puke
items.take: Copper just had its worst daily drop in more than a year, about 6%, as investors reassess AI data-center spending, a second crack in the buildout trade beyond Nvidia. Today's slate: jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey at 8:30 a.m., with the October jobs report out Friday.
